raw_text:
The objective of this research is to examine why sites using the same nominal work process exhibit persistent completion-time differences and to identify measurable factors contributing to these differences. This involves identifying observable phenomena that can distinguish between competing explanations for these differences.

Assumptions
It is assumed that work processes, as documented, are consistent across sites.
It is also assumed that completion times are relevant and manipulable variables.

Research design
The research design employs a software-testing methodological approach, focusing on process mining and performance measurement. Process mining will be used to model the nominal work process, and statistical methods will be used to measure and analyze completion-time differences. Ten sites will be randomly selected for detailed study, and observations will be made during normal operation to gather data.

Data or evidence needed
- Historical records of work process implementations at the selected sites.
- Real-time data on completion times.
- Observational notes on operational practices.

Measurement
- Completion times will be measured over several identical work cycles.
- Process mining will be used to model standard and actual work flows.
- Observational metrics (e.g., communication frequencies, resource allocation efficiency) will be recorded.

Analysis
- Statistical analysis will be conducted to identify factors significantly associated with variations in completion times.
- Process mining tools will be used to compare modeled versus actual work flows.

Decision / stopping rule
The research will continue until a consensus is reached on the key factors contributing to completion-time differences, or until all predefined criteria for data collection and analysis are satisfied.

Limitations
The study may encounter difficulties with direct observation limitations or observer bias. Variability in operational practices may also confound the analysis. It is critical to use robust statistical methods to control for these limitations.
